overview: Constantine Bay is a big, sandy beach about three miles west of Padstow, one of the string of lovely beaches along this stretch of the north coast between Trevose Head and Porthcothan. It faces west into the Atlantic and is popular with surfers, with lifeguards in summer.
Behind the beach is a large dune system, which is fragile and protected, so stick to the marked paths through it.

expect.title: Sand and surf
expect.text: A large, sandy beach that picks up Atlantic swell, with lifeguard patrols in summer.

expect.title: Dunes
expect.text: Big dunes back the beach, part of a protected site for its plants and geology.

expect.title: Trevose Head
expect.text: The headland and its lighthouse are a short walk north along the coast path.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: About three miles west of Padstow, in the parish of St Merryn.

goodToKnow.label: The dunes
goodToKnow.text: They’re protected and suffering from erosion, so please keep to the paths.

week.text: A classic north-coast beach day near Padstow. It faces west, so it’s a good spot to stay on for the sunset, and you can hop between neighbouring beaches like Treyarnon and Booby’s Bay along the coast path.

pairWith.why: a wilder beach just to the north
the headland lighthouse for a walk with views

tips: Stay for sunset: the beach faces straight out to the west.
